title: Classification Tasks with Local and Global Resource Allocation Constraints
authors: Danit Abukasis Shifman, Itay Margolin, Chen Halfi, Gonen Singer
conclusions: Proposes a two-phase framework: Phase 1 trains an ML classifier to produce a probability matrix; Phase 2 solves a linear program (with an OR-Tools GLOP solver) that allocates the capped labels using that probability matrix and a per-sample misclassification cost matrix.

Defines two distinct resource-constraint types: target-based (global cap on total items assigned to a class) and feature-based (local cap on items from a subgroup/subset assigned to a class) — the feature-based type is claimed as new to the classification-constraint literature.

Proves the LP's constraint coefficient matrix is totally unimodular (via Ghouila-Houri's characterization), so the LP relaxation always yields an integer optimal allocation without needing an explicit integer program.
Introduces a naive greedy heuristic (Algorithm 1, expected-cost sorted assignment) as a fast baseline/comparator to the LP.

Empirically (student-dropout tabular dataset, decision tree / random forest / perfect classifier, 10-fold CV), the LP framework beats the naive heuristic on cost and accuracy by a statistically significant margin (paired t-test), with larger gains under looser target-based constraints (0.5-0.8) than under tight ones (0.2-0.3).

Scope is explicitly tabular/decision-support (student tutoring allocation); paper notes extension to other data types (e.g., images) and to influence-on-future-predictions as future work, not something it studies.
our_use: Cited three times as the source of the 'local-plus-global' (target-based + feature-based) constraint structure that our TraLO also uses (main.tex:190-193, related work), and as the origin of our post-hoc 'Shifman-LP' baseline: a deploy-time LP clipper applied to a trained model's test-set softmax that allocates capped labels under global+local caps (main.tex:200-205, 352-354), explicitly noted as an adaptation that swaps the paper's general misclassification cost matrix for an identity cost (main.tex:376-379).
issues: none — title, full author list/order, journal name, volume(59)/number(1)/pages(61-66)/year(2025), DOI, and publisher all verified against the PDF front matter and match exactly.
